title: International Development Association
definition: The International Development Association (IDA) is the concessional financing arm of the World Bank Group that helps the world’s poorest countries by providing zero- to low-interest loans (called credits) and grants for programs that boost economic growth, reduce poverty, and improve people’s lives.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial microtopic under Economy (External Sector & International Organizations). Frequently tested in Prelims regarding World Bank Group membership, concessional lending windows, eligibility criteria (GNI per capita thresholds), and India's historical and current status (both as a former major borrower and now as a donor).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of International Development Association.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Bretton Woods institutions and World Bank Group entities.
